supports.excerpt:
```
getExecutionEnvironment()

createLocalEnvironment()

createRemoteEnvironment(host: String, port: Int, jarFiles: String*)

```

For specifying data sources the execution environment has several methods to
read from files using various methods: you can just read them line by line, as
CSV files, or using any of the other provided sources. To just read a text file
as a sequence of lines, you can use:

```
val env = StreamExecutionEnvironment.getExecutionEnvironment()

val text: DataStream[String] = env.readTextFile("file:///path/to/file")

```

This will give you a DataStream on which you can then apply transformations to
create new derived DataStreams.

You apply transformations by calling methods on DataStream with a
transformation functions. For example, a map transformation looks like this:

```
val input: DataSet[String] = ...

val mapped = input.map { x => x.toInt }

```

This will create a new DataStream by converting every String in the original
collection to an Integer.

Once you have a DataStream containing your final results, you can write it to
an outside system by creating a sink. These are just some example methods for
creating a sink:

```
writeAsText(path: String)

print()

```

Once you specified the complete program you need to trigger the program
execution by calling `execute()` on the `StreamExecutionEnvironment`.
Depending on the type of the `ExecutionEnvironment` the execution will be
triggered on your local machine or submit your program for execution on a
cluster.

The `execute()` method will wait for the job to finish and then return a
`JobExecutionResult`, this contains execution times and accumulator results.

```
final JobClient jobClient = env.executeAsync();

final JobExecutionResult jobExecutionResult = jobClient.getJobExecutionResult().get();

```

skill_drafts.name: StreamExecutionEnvironment Setup
skill_drafts.description: Initialize and configure a Flink StreamExecutionEnvironment for local or remote execution. Establishes the entry point for defining and executing streaming data pipelines.
skill_drafts.objective: Set up execution context for streaming job
applicable_signals: Need to specify execution mode (local vs. remote)
contraindications: Batch processing jobs (use DataSet API instead)
Reusing an existing StreamExecutionEnvironment from another scope
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Choose execution mode', 'detail': 'Decide between getExecutionEnvironment() (auto-detect), createLocalEnvironment() (local), or createRemoteEnvironment() (cluster)'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Instantiate environment', 'detail': 'Call the selected method with appropriate parameters (host, port, jar files for remote mode)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Verify environment is active', 'detail': 'Confirm the returned StreamExecutionEnvironment instance is non-null and ready to accept sources'}
triggers: Starting a new Flink streaming application
Switching between local development and cluster deployment
Initializing a streaming pipeline before defining sources
constraints: Must be called before defining data sources or transformations
Remote environment requires valid host and port parameters
JAR files must be accessible at specified paths for remote execution
cautions: Ensure network connectivity and cluster availability before using createRemoteEnvironment()
JAR file paths must be absolute or resolvable from the execution context
Local environment is suitable only for development and testing, not production
output_contract: Returns an active StreamExecutionEnvironment instance ready to accept data sources via readTextFile(), readFile(), or other source methods, and ready to apply transformations and sinks.

metadata.prompt: Call getExecutionEnvironment() to obtain the default execution environment, createLocalEnvironment() for local development, or createRemoteEnvironment(host, port, jarFiles) to connect to a remote cluster. The resulting StreamExecutionEnvironment instance is the foundation for all subsequent data source definitions and transformations.

skill_drafts.name: DataStream Source Reading
skill_drafts.description: Read data from external file sources (text files, CSV) into a typed DataStream object for processing. Converts raw input into a transformable stream ready for downstream operations.
skill_drafts.objective: Ingest data from file-based sources into a streaming pipeline as a reusable DataStream
applicable_signals: Need to read text files line-by-line into a stream
CSV or other file-based source data must be ingested
Initial data source for a streaming pipeline is a local or remote file
contraindications: Data already exists as an in-memory DataStream
Using Kafka, message queue, or other streaming source connectors
Batch processing with DataSet API instead of DataStream
intervention_moves: Obtain or create a StreamExecutionEnvironment instance
Call readTextFile(path) or appropriate source method with file URI
Assign result to a typed DataStream variable
Verify DataStream is ready for chaining transformations
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Initialize StreamExecutionEnvironment', 'detail': 'Call getExecutionEnvironment(), createLocalEnvironment(), or createRemoteEnvironment()'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Call source reading method', 'detail': 'Use env.readTextFile(path) to read text file line-by-line into DataStream[String]'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Assign to typed variable', 'detail': 'Store result as val text: DataStream[String] = env.readTextFile(...)'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify stream is ready', 'detail': 'Confirm DataStream object is created and ready for transformations or sinks'}
triggers: Need to read text files, CSV, or other file-based sources as the initial data stream
constraints: File path must be accessible (local or remote URI format)
Source method must match data format (text, CSV, etc.)
Execution environment must be initialized before calling source methods
cautions: File I/O may block; ensure file is available before execution
Large files may require memory and parallelism tuning
Path format must follow URI scheme (file://, hdfs://, etc.)
output_contract: Returns a typed DataStream[T] object (e.g., DataStream[String] for text files) that is ready to accept downstream transformations (map, filter, etc.) or be written to a sink. The stream represents the complete sequence of records from the source file.

metadata.prompt: Use StreamExecutionEnvironment methods to read from file-based sources. Call readTextFile() or equivalent source method on the execution environment, passing the file path. The result is a typed DataStream[T] that can be passed to transformations (map, filter, etc.) or sinks.

skill_drafts.name: DataStream Transformation Application
skill_drafts.description: Apply transformation functions (map, filter, flatMap, etc.) to a DataStream to create derived streams. Chains transformations to build processing logic by calling methods on DataStream objects.
skill_drafts.objective: Transform and derive new DataStreams from input data using element-wise or aggregation functions
applicable_signals: Transformation logic is defined (map, filter, flatMap, etc.)
Downstream sink or further transformation is planned
contraindications: No transformation needed; data already in final form
Transformation function is undefined or invalid
workflow_steps: Obtain or reference an existing DataStream[T]
Define the transformation function (map, filter, flatMap, etc.)
Call the transformation method on the DataStream with the function
Capture the resulting DataStream[U]
Chain additional transformations or proceed to sink
triggers: DataStream is available and requires element-wise transformation
Need to convert, filter, or aggregate stream elements
constraints: Transformation function must be compatible with input element type
Output type U must be serializable
Chained transformations must maintain type compatibility
cautions: Each transformation creates a new DataStream; original stream is not modified
Complex nested transformations may impact performance; consider optimization
Type mismatches in chained transformations will cause runtime errors
output_contract: Returns a new DataStream[U] with transformation logic applied, ready for further chaining, sinking, or execution

metadata.prompt: To transform a DataStream, call transformation methods on the DataStream object with a transformation function. For example, use map to convert each element: `val mapped = input.map { x => x.toInt }`. This creates a new DataStream by applying the function to every element in the original stream. Chain multiple transformations to build complex processing logic.

skill_drafts.name: DataStream Sink Writing
skill_drafts.description: Write processed DataStream results to external systems (files, stdout, databases). Finalizes the pipeline by persisting or outputting results.
skill_drafts.objective: Output final DataStream results to external sink
applicable_signals: Caller has target output path or destination
contraindications: Results not yet finalized or validated
Sink already attached to this DataStream
intervention_moves: Call writeAsText(path: String) to write DataStream to file
Call print() to output DataStream to console/stdout
Attach sink before calling execute() on StreamExecutionEnvironment
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Obtain final DataStream after all transformations', 'detail': 'Ensure all map, filter, and other transformations are complete'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Choose sink method based on output destination', 'detail': 'Use writeAsText(path) for file output or print() for console output'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Call sink method on final DataStream', 'detail': 'Example: finalStream.writeAsText("file:///path/to/output") or finalStream.print()'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Trigger execution', 'detail': 'Call env.execute() or env.executeAsync() to start the pipeline and write results'}
triggers: Final DataStream containing processed results is ready
Need to persist results to external system
constraints: Sink must be attached to final DataStream, not intermediate streams
execute() or executeAsync() must be called after sink attachment to trigger output
File paths must be valid and writable
cautions: Calling sink on intermediate DataStream may cause unexpected output
Without execute(), sink is configured but not executed
Multiple sinks can be attached to same DataStream for multiple outputs
output_contract: Sink is configured and attached to DataStream; ready for execution. Upon execute(), results are written to specified external system (file or stdout). JobExecutionResult returned contains execution metadata.

examples.output: writeAsText("file:///output/results.txt") attaches sink; execute() writes results to file
examples.notes: File path must be accessible; output format is one record per line

examples.output: print() attaches sink; execute() outputs results to console
examples.notes: Useful for testing and debugging; all records printed to stdout

metadata.prompt: After all transformations are complete, attach a sink to the DataStream to write results to an external system. Use writeAsText(path) to write to a file or print() to output to console. The sink must be called on the final DataStream before execute() is invoked.

skill_drafts.name: Job Execution and Result Retrieval
skill_drafts.description: Trigger a Flink streaming job execution and retrieve execution results including timing and accumulator metrics. Supports both synchronous and asynchronous execution modes.
skill_drafts.objective: Execute streaming job and collect execution metadata
applicable_signals: All transformations and sinks are attached
contraindications: Sinks not yet attached to DataStream
intervention_moves: Invoke execute() for blocking execution with immediate result
Invoke executeAsync() for non-blocking execution with JobClient callback
Call getJobExecutionResult().get() on JobClient to await and retrieve results
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Verify pipeline is complete with all transformations and sinks attached'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Choose execution mode: call execute() for synchronous or executeAsync() for asynchronous'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'If using executeAsync(), obtain JobClient and call getJobExecutionResult().get() to retrieve results'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Inspect JobExecutionResult for execution times and accumulator values'}
triggers: Pipeline definition is complete and ready to run; need to start job and monitor execution results
constraints: StreamExecutionEnvironment must be instantiated before calling execute() or executeAsync()
All DataStream transformations must be defined before execution
At least one sink must be attached to the pipeline
cautions: Synchronous execute() blocks until job completion; use executeAsync() for non-blocking behavior in interactive environments
JobClient.getJobExecutionResult().get() is a blocking call; consider timeout handling in production
output_contract: Returns JobExecutionResult containing execution times, accumulator results, and job completion status. Synchronous execute() returns result directly; asynchronous executeAsync() returns JobClient from which result is retrieved via getJobExecutionResult().get().

examples.input: StreamExecutionEnvironment with complete pipeline (source → transformations → sink)
examples.output: JobExecutionResult with execution duration and accumulator metrics

examples.input: StreamExecutionEnvironment with complete pipeline, non-blocking requirement
examples.output: JobClient object; calling getJobExecutionResult().get() yields JobExecutionResult

metadata.prompt: Call execute() for synchronous execution or executeAsync() for non-blocking execution on the StreamExecutionEnvironment. Synchronous execute() waits for job completion and returns JobExecutionResult directly. Asynchronous executeAsync() returns a JobClient; call getJobExecutionResult().get() on the client to retrieve the final JobExecutionResult containing execution times and accumulator values.
